title: DNA Purification from an Agarose Gel Using NucleoSpin® PCR Clean-up Kit
author: Alba Balletbó
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7hrhj56
materials: NucleoSpin® PCR clean-up Gel extraction kit

steps.title: Excise DNA band under UV
steps.instruction: Place the gel in an open UV box while wearing proper UV eye protection, optionally on a glass plate to protect the box, remove the gel from its plastic tray, and with a clean sterile razor blade slice out the desired DNA fragment, trimming excess gel from top, bottom and sides as much as possible.

steps.title: Transfer gel slice to tube
steps.instruction: Place the excised gel fragment into a labeled micro‑fuge tube.

steps.title: Weigh gel to determine volume
steps.instruction: Zero a balance with an empty tube, then weigh the tube containing the gel slice (or subtract the weight of an empty tube) to obtain the gel weight, which is proportional to its liquid volume and will be used to calculate buffer volumes.

steps.title: Add binding buffer
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL Binding Buffer (NTI) for every 100 mg of gel measured.

steps.title: Melt gel at 50 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 50 °C for 5–10 minutes or until the agarose has completely melted.

steps.title: Prepare spin column
steps.instruction: Place a NucleoSpin® PCR clean‑up Gel column into the provided 2 mL collection tube.

steps.title: Load sample onto column
steps.instruction: Apply up to 700 µL of the DNA/agarose solution to the column and centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 30 seconds at room temperature. For volumes >700 µL, repeat loading and centrifugation in 700 µL increments. Each column can bind up to 25 µg DNA; split the sample into additional columns if a larger yield is expected.

steps.title: Wash column with Buffer NT3
steps.instruction: Add 700 µL Buffer NT3 to the column, centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 30 seconds at room temperature, discard the flow‑through, and reuse the same collection tube. Repeat with a second 700 µL of Buffer NT3.

steps.title: Dry column matrix
steps.instruction: Discard any remaining liquid and centrifuge the empty column for 1 minute at 11 000 × g at room temperature to remove residual ethanol.

steps.title: Elute purified DNA
steps.instruction: Transfer the column to a clean 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, add 15–30 µL Elution Buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8.5) directly onto the matrix, incubate 1 minute at room temperature, then centrifuge 1 minute at 11 000 × g to collect the eluate (≈70 % of bound DNA). An optional second elution with the same volume can be performed for residual DNA, though at lower concentration.
